hook: Why Can't AI Count Letters in 'Strawberry'? 🍓
headline: Why AI Can Count to Billions But Fails at Strawberry 'r's

slides.speaker: byte
slides.title: Why Can't AI Count 'r's? 🍓
slides.bubble: Why does ChatGPT struggle to count how many 'r's are in 'strawberry'?

slides.speaker: vj
slides.title: Subword Tokenization 🧩
slides.bubble: Because LLMs never see letters! Words are chopped into numeric chunks called tokens.

slides.speaker: byte
slides.title: Token Blindspot 🕶️
slides.bubble: So the word 'strawberry' isn't stored as ten individual characters?

slides.speaker: vj
slides.title: Tokens Over Letters 🔢
slides.bubble: Right! It sees token IDs like 'straw' and 'berry', completely hiding the raw letters.

slides.speaker: byte
slides.title: How Do Newer AIs Fix It? ⚡
slides.bubble: Can reasoning models fix this by spelling out the word internally?

slides.speaker: vj
slides.title: Chain-of-Thought Power 🧠
slides.bubble: Yes! Reasoning models spell each letter in their scratchpad to count accurately.

slides.speaker: byte
slides.title: Mind-Blowing Fact 💡
slides.bubble: Follow @vijayakumarj_ai for daily mind-blowing tech facts!

takeaway: AI doesn't see letters—it sees token chunks. Asking for letter counts breaks subword tokenization!
caption:
🧠 DID YOU KNOW? 🤯

Why can AI solve differential equations but fail to count letters in 'strawberry'?

Here is the answer:
🔹 Language models do not read individual characters.
🔹 Words are tokenized into subword IDs (e.g. 'straw' + 'berry').
🔹 Without seeing individual letters, character counting becomes a statistical guess!
